title: Medical Emergency & Disaster First Aid Guide
summary: Quick first aid saves lives in disaster emergencies. Check scene safety, assess responsiveness, and call emergency medical aid.
precautions: Ensure scene safety before approaching any injured victim (check for live wires, falling debris, or gas fumes).
Use personal protective equipment (gloves, masks) if available to avoid blood-borne exposure.
Call 108 or the local Ambulance Service immediately.
evacuation: Do NOT move victims with suspected spinal or head trauma unless there is immediate life-threatening danger (fire, rising water).
Use a firm stretcher or improvised wooden board for spinal immobilization when evacuation is mandatory.
firstAid: Severe Bleeding: Apply firm, continuous direct pressure to the wound with a clean cloth or bandage. Elevate limb above heart level.
Unresponsive & Not Breathing: Start CPR immediately — 30 chest compressions followed by 2 rescue breaths.
Choking: Perform abdominal thrusts (Heimlich maneuver) until blockage is cleared.
Fractures: Immobilize bone above and below the fracture site using splints and soft padding.
Heatstroke / Dehydration: Move victim to shade, loosen tight clothing, and offer small sips of ORS (Oral Rehydration Solution) or clean water.
emergencyChecklist: Sterile gauze pads and adhesive bandages
dos: DO call emergency medical services (108) early.
DO keep injured victims calm and warm.
DO apply direct pressure to stop heavy bleeding.
donts: DON'T move victims with back/neck pain unnecessarily.
DON'T give food or liquids to an unconscious person.
DON'T remove impaled objects from wounds; stabilize them in place.
